independentAnswers.reasoning: Avoiding drawn obstacles does not satisfy a minimum turning-radius limit; the route fails robot-specific feasibility.
The dashed geometric route illustrates obstacle avoidance only; no competing-path optimization proof or swept finite-body clearance is depicted.
Safety corresponds to avoiding damage, efficiency to saving battery, and autonomy to operating without continual intervention.
An acceleration ceiling is a hard dynamic feasibility constraint, whereas energy is an objective over the feasible set.
Compare each objective independently:8m<10m selectsP, while9J<12J selectsQ. Feasibility does not collapse the objectives.
The obstacle/free-space digital map is environment representation, distinct from endpoints, constraints and selection criterion.
Repeated patrol for change detection is surveillance/monitoring; acquiring an unknown layout is exploration.
Coffee handover requires a feasible, smooth end-effector trajectory respecting intermediate configurations and dynamic limits, not endpoint reachability alone.
UAV paths occupy3Dairspace and must respect both physical obstacles and the explicitly stated restricted region.
City traffic contains moving obstacles, so a static route cannot replace current observations and reactive collision handling.
The actual figure has arrows labeled feedback from both perception and localization into planning.
The figure labels planning to execution as plan, and execution to controller/actuator as command.
Obstacle mapping is perception; estimating pose relative to that map is localization under the slide's functional distinction.
An estimate can retain measurement/model uncertainty; exact-position wording must not be interpreted as an infallibility guarantee.
The source localization list explicitly contains GPS,IMU,wheel encoders andSLAM. The separate list is not an exclusive real-world sensor taxonomy.
The long A-B map route depicts global planning and the magnified pothole maneuver depicts local avoidance.
A route over the whole map remains global in scope even if recomputed during motion; the offline contrast is a baseline example rather than a logical restriction.
Long-range destination guidance and short-range responses to nearby changes address complementary planning needs.
The displayed global column names Dijkstra's algorithm and A-star, not the other listed pairings.
The simplified binary map labels1occupied and0free;1does not mean unknown or unit traversal cost.
Counting the actual grid yields16occupied cells in64total, hence48free vertices with no start-reachability filtering.
The coarse grid is40by20=800cells;the fine grid80by40=3200cells. At one byte per cell this is a fourfold increase.
A1.0mrequired width exceeds0.8mcorridor width, independent of finer discretization or graph representation. Free centerline is insufficient.
The place graph directly stores node connectivity and route costs, while omitting fine metric obstacle boundary detail.
The actual diagonal arrow isCtoBwithcost7;there is no drawn BtoC reverse edge.
Enumerating all five directed terminal paths gives ABE4,ACBE9,ACDE10,ABDE15,ACBDE20. ABE is the unique cheapest.
Changing the edge metric changes the optimization objective to summed modeled travel time; shortest geometric distance need not coincide.
Greedy local weights chooseAC1,CD2,DE7,total10. The unchosen AB3,BE1 route totals4, demonstrating lack of lookahead.
Four-connected means four side neighbors; eight-connected additionally includes the four corner neighbors of an unobstructed interior cell.
Two cardinal moves contribute1m;three diagonal moves contribute1.5sqrt2m,total3.121320...m. This is sequence length, not displacement.
Only free, reachable transitions satisfying the connectivity and robot motion assumptions belong in the search graph.
Both side cells are blocked,so the supplied no-corner-cutting rule forbids the only candidate diagonal; no cardinal path exists inside the2by2grid.
BFS minimizes the number of edges, not a weighted sum. Cardinal1anddiagonal sqrt2break equality between hop count and cost,without implying every result is wrong.
The depicted directed graph is acyclic and every nonterminal vertex has an outgoing route toE. Full enumeration gives at most four moves,not universal optimality.
Ahas two outgoing arrows andBhas two;the supplied independent uniform choices giveP(A-B-E)=1/2times1/2=1/4,not one fifth from counting whole paths.
The procedure pops the initial start,tests the goal,and stops before successor expansion. The empty path has zero cost.
Exhaustive failure on the finite fixed graph rules out a graph route,not a physical passage omitted by the representation.
Bwas already explored,Ealready queued,andGis new;retainEandFandappendGonce to obtain[E,F,G].
After expandingS,the queue containsG2andA3;goal-on-removal stops at2 before revealing the negative A-G edge. The alternative S-A-G costs1 and there is no cycle.
Independent reverse shortest-path computation yieldsA9,B7,C7,D6,E4,F3,G0km;BusesB-E-F-G7 andDhas a6kmminimum via directG orE-F-G.
The true remaining distance fromEis1+3=4km,so5overestimates. A8<=9,B7=7,F3=3are admissible values for their separate candidates.
No route edge has been traversed,so g(A)=0km;f(A)=g+h=0+7=7km.
The inspected example has three versus six non-goal expansions and equal9kmoptimal routes. Expansion counts alone neither prove elapsed-time ratios nor universal speedups.
